programme.title: Camanachd air BBC ALBA/Shinty on BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Cupa Comann Ceilteach Ghlaschu beò à Pàirce Peterson ann an Glaschu le Glaschu Meadhan Earra-Ghàidheal a’ cluiche Camanachd an Òbain sa chuairt dheireannaich. ‘S iad Camanachd an Òbain a bhuannaich an-uiridh agus tha iad ag amas air a’ chupa a ghlèidheadh airson an ceithreamh bliadhna sreath a chèile. Làn aithris air a' gheama bho Mìcheal Steele agus Katie Drain. The Glasgow Celtic Society Challenge Cup final live from Peterson Park, between Glasgow Mid Argyll and Oban Camanachd. Oban are looking to retain the cup they won last year for the fourth successive season. Full match commentary from Micheal Steele and Katie Drain.

programme.title: Somhairle Spins
programme.desc: Tha slighe dùbhlanach aig Somhairle agus a bhràthair Innes air a’ chiad latha aca a’ rothaireachd eadar Inbhir Nis agus Glaschu air an Badger Divide. Somhairle and his brother Innes have a challenging start on their first day cycling between Inverness and Glasgow on the Badger Divide.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: An Sgoth
programme.desc: Se obair la toiseachadh agus b'e obair bliadhna a bh'ann an sgoth Niseach a chriochnachadh. Tha am program seo a' leanntainn an obair togail , na daoine a bha sas ann ag urachadh seann sgillean agus nab ha a-mach is a-steach a'ceilidh oirre. In 1994 work began in Lewis to construct a special boat using traditional skills. The Sgoth was the traditional fishing boat of the Ness district of Lewis and this film follows the year-long project to construct a sea-worthy vessel.

programme.title: Brunch le Abigail
programme.desc: Tha Abigail a’ dèanamh Overnight Oats le Sùbhagan is Piostaisean, math airson deagh bhracaist aig an taigh no airson a thoirt leat dhan oifis. Abigail makes raspberry and pistachio overnight oats, ideal for a breakfast snack, or to take with you to the office. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Suas gu Deas
programme.desc: Se latha geamaichean Uibhist a Deas a th’ann agus tha farpais iasgaich ann am Barraigh. A fishing competition is held in Barra, while Highland dancers compete at the South Uist games.

programme.title: Port Steòrnabhaigh
programme.desc: Based in the main port in the Hebrides, we follow the beating hearts of Stornoway Harbour. In her shelter, there is a bustling community to be found. In this episode, we see the final preparations for the arrival of the first cruise ship at the Deep Water Terminal, and the town centre gets a facelift with some new additions. Stèidhte ann am prìomh port nan Eilean Siar, the sinne a’ leantainn cridhe Port Steòrnabhaigh. Na fasgadh, tha coimhearsnachd trang ri lorg. Anns a’ phrògram seo, tha an obair steidheachaidh mu dheireadh a’ tachairt leis a’ chiad chrùs aig a’ Chala Dhomhain air fàire, agus leasachadh air meadhan baile Steòrnabhaigh. Thig còmhla rinn ‘s sinn a’ leanntainn beatha ann am Port Steòrnabhaigh.

programme.title: Seirm
programme.desc: Ceòl dùthchasach agus traidiseanta air a lìbhrigeadh le Màiri Anna NicUalraig. Chaidh Seirm Celtic Connections a’ chlàradh ann an 2022 agus tha an ceathramh prògram seo a’ foillseachadh iomadachd na fèise tro thaisbeanaidhean le Leyla McCalla, Dlù, Stundom, Norman Blake, James Grant and Monica Queen. Traditional music show presented by Mary Ann Kennedy. Seirm Celtic Connections was filmed in 2022 and this episode reflects the diversity of the festival. With appearances by Leyla McCalla, Dlù, Stundom, plus Norman Blake, James Grant and Monica Queen.

programme.title: Baile na h-Ola (Aberdeen: When Oil Came to Town)
programme.desc: Dhòirt an airgead a-steach, ach chan eil dìleab na h-ola ri fhaicinn ’s a bhaile an-diugh. Fifty years of oil has had a significant impact on Aberdeen, but what is the legacy?

programme.title: Rurachd (Foraging)
programme.desc: Mary Ann Kennedy and Lucy Cooke drum up a foraged feast with friends at the Wildluing Observatory in Argyll.

programme.title: An Cruinne Caochlaideach/Dynamic Planet
programme.desc: As the ice drastically melts, we see how science, nature and tradition can prepare us for the future.

programme.title: Belladrum
programme.desc: Tha Fiona NicChoinnich is Niall Iain Dòmhnallach a’ cur fàilt’ oirbh chun a’ chiad latha aig Belladrum 2025. Anns a’ phrògram seo, bidh an seinneadair cliùiteach Paul Heaton, a bha soirbheachail mar phrìomh sheinneadair dhen bhuidheann indie rock bho na 80an, The Housemartins. Cuide ri Paul air Àrd-Ùrlar Hot House tha Rianne Downey aige air aoigheachd, airson an oidhche a thoirt gu ceann. Fiona MacKenzie and Niall Iain Macdonald welcome you to the first day at Belladrum 2025. This programme features renowned singer Paul Heaton, who was successful as the lead singer of 80s indie rock group The Housemartins. Joining Paul on the Hot House Stage to bring the night to a close is special guest Rianne Downey.

programme.title: Making Life on Earth: Attenborough's Greatest Adventure
programme.desc: In 1976, David Attenborough embarked on his most ambitious project ever, Life on Earth. No-one had ever attempted a natural history series on this scale before, and David’s reputation was on the line. This is the remarkable story behind the BBC’s most famous wildlife blockbuster: a three-year, hair-raising odyssey around the world, travelling to 40 countries and filming over 600 species, including the famous mountain gorillas. First broadcast in 1979 and watched by 500 million people, it launched David Attenborough’s career as the most successful and influential wildlife film-maker of our time.

Martin Sharkey explores how changes in the way we watch content are shaping new technologies. Paul Carter hits the racetrack to see if AI technology systems can make journeys safer, and Andrew Rogers meets the dogs being helped to walk and run again thanks to assistive mobility aids.

programme.title: China's Greatest Treasures
programme.desc: Across the world, fashion is a fundamental expression of who we are. Today, people in China are rediscovering the beauty of their extraordinarily rich clothing heritage. In this programme, Alastair discovers how historic fashion design still resonates with people in China today, and how it has become a way in which people can celebrate their identity.

programme.title: World Questions
programme.desc: A special edition of World Questions, putting young Moroccan women at the centre of a national debate about rights, faith and family law reform. Jonny Dymond chairs a panel of feminist activists and conservatives as they debate issues such as child marriage, sex outside marriage, inheritance, harassment and polygamy. As a new generation pushes for change, Morocco stands out in the Muslim world, with reform being debated openly, and this programme hears from young women at a pivotal moment in civil society.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: Following the sentencing of 13 people for violent disorder during protests in Southampton, attention has turned to the role of content creators who film demonstrations and public disorder. The judge cited the usefulness of footage filmed by so-called 'citizen journalists'. Siddharth Venkataramakrishnan of the Institute for Strategic Dialogue and content creator Wesley Winter give their perspective on the issue. The BBC has begun setting out changes as part of plans to deliver significant savings across the organisation. The measures include the closure of several programmes across radio and current affairs output, alongside wider reductions in staffing. Jonathan Munro, global director of BBC News, outlines the changes. Norma Percy has spent years getting to the heart of some of the biggest moments in recent history. Her documentaries have been celebrated for talking directly to the people who made the decisions. As the BBC airs her latest film - about Brexit - she reflects on her storied career and the future of documentary-making.

programme.title: The Travel Show
programme.desc: Train enthusiast Francis Bourgeois travels to Malaysia to explore a railway network dating back 140 years. Jumping on board the iconic Jungle Railway, he experiences one of Southeast Asia's most spectacular train journeys, before arriving in the bustling capital city, Kuala Lumpur, and finishing up on Penang Island for their spectacular Lunar New Year celebrations. En route he joins forces with some of Malaysia's train devotees, finding a shared and nostalgic affection for the country's older, and less common freight trains.

This isn’t going to end well.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: The gang belatedly get involved in the Great Famine, the one thing they didn’t need to get involved in. Callum’s new job at the Ballymac Folk Museum sends him down a spiral of method acting as a starving peasant. And he’s helped along in this grovelling subservience by his new boss, tyrannical land steward Phillip. The sudden news, to Jordan, that a million people died during the potato famine causes him to finally develop empathy, and it turns out to be a real pain.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: Strange things are afoot in Ballymacnoose: animals in small clothing, paranormal sightings of leprechauns, and most bizarrely of all, Callum gets his first ever match on a dating app. The one prickle on the pickle is that Gwen, Callum’s dream girl, is also in an open relationship with the 50-year-old Grainne, a woman who disembowels chickens for a living. Meanwhile, Gemma becomes obsessed with dressing farm animals in tiny clothing and causes Sammy to spin out in paranoia thinking that his farm has become infested with leprechauns. So Lorcan has no other choice but to introduce Gemma to the dark secrets of the Ballymacnoose Paranormal Society, also run by his da and Frank.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: Life in Ballymacnoose becomes very complicated when Callum accidentally walks in on Gemma and Lorcan trying out a new form of lovemaking. The sight triggers a long-buried childhood trauma in Callum and raises uncomfortable questions about the town’s deeply repressed relationship with sex. Can Ballymacnoose open its heart to true love? Meanwhile, Jordan has officially begun dating his much older lover, 50-year-old Grainne. But as their relationship deepens, Jordan is confronted with another harsh reality of adulthood: he’s going bald. Faced with the slow retreat of his hairline and the love of a good woman, Jordan must decide whether to cling to denial or embrace manhood in all its forms - love, responsibility and mushroom carbonaras.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: As Callum begins slowly unravelling under the strain of Jordan's relentless night terrors about baldness, he stumbles upon a flyer for Ballymacbot Wars - a local robot combat tournament offering a generous cash prize and potential ticket out of Jordan’s bedroom. Meanwhile, Jordan is uncharacteristically uninterested in the whole affair. He's become a bald hermit, terrified to leave the house and expose his creamy scalp to the outside world. That is, until, like a dagger in the night, a hooded burst of inspiration sends him back out into the world… and the robot wars.

programme.title: Pointless Celebrities
programme.desc: A special cricket edition of the general knowledge quiz in which four teams try to come up with the answers that no-one else could think of. Presented by Alexander Armstrong and co-host Richard Osman, with contestants Alison Mitchell, Andy Zaltzman, Devon Malcolm, Graham Gooch, Georgie Heath, Fran Wilson, Graeme Swann and Mark Ramprakash.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage as World Cup debutants Curacao play their second match in Group E against Ecuador at Kansas City Stadium. Curacao are the smallest nation ever to qualify for a World Cup and have the oldest coach in the tournament's history: 78-year-old former Rangers and Sunderland manager Dick Advocaat. Ecuador impressively finished second in South American qualifying and boast Chelsea midfielder Moises Caicedo in their ranks. It’s 20 years since their best performance at a World Cup, making the last 16 in 2006, when they were knocked out by England.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: Strange things are afoot in Ballymacnoose: animals in small clothing, paranormal sightings of leprechauns, and most bizarrely of all, Callum gets his first ever match on a dating app. The one prickle on the pickle is that Gwen, Callum’s dream girl, is also in an open relationship with the 50-year-old Grainne, a woman who disembowels chickens for a living. Meanwhile, Gemma becomes obsessed with dressing farm animals in tiny clothing and causes Sammy to spin out in paranoia thinking that his farm has become infested with leprechauns. So Lorcan has no other choice but to introduce Gemma to the dark secrets of the Ballymacnoose Paranormal Society, also run by his da and Frank.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: Life in Ballymacnoose becomes very complicated when Callum accidentally walks in on Gemma and Lorcan trying out a new form of lovemaking. The sight triggers a long-buried childhood trauma in Callum and raises uncomfortable questions about the town’s deeply repressed relationship with sex. Can Ballymacnoose open its heart to true love? Meanwhile, Jordan has officially begun dating his much older lover, 50-year-old Grainne. But as their relationship deepens, Jordan is confronted with another harsh reality of adulthood: he’s going bald. Faced with the slow retreat of his hairline and the love of a good woman, Jordan must decide whether to cling to denial or embrace manhood in all its forms - love, responsibility and mushroom carbonaras.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: As Callum begins slowly unravelling under the strain of Jordan's relentless night terrors about baldness, he stumbles upon a flyer for Ballymacbot Wars - a local robot combat tournament offering a generous cash prize and potential ticket out of Jordan’s bedroom. Meanwhile, Jordan is uncharacteristically uninterested in the whole affair. He's become a bald hermit, terrified to leave the house and expose his creamy scalp to the outside world. That is, until, like a dagger in the night, a hooded burst of inspiration sends him back out into the world… and the robot wars.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage as World Cup debutants Curacao play their second match in Group E against Ecuador at Kansas City Stadium. Curacao are the smallest nation ever to qualify for a World Cup and have the oldest coach in the tournament's history: 78-year-old former Rangers and Sunderland manager Dick Advocaat. Ecuador impressively finished second in South American qualifying and boast Chelsea midfielder Moises Caicedo in their ranks. It’s 20 years since their best performance at a World Cup, making the last 16 in 2006, when they were knocked out by England.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: The gang belatedly get involved in the Great Famine, the one thing they didn’t need to get involved in. Callum’s new job at the Ballymac Folk Museum sends him down a spiral of method acting as a starving peasant. And he’s helped along in this grovelling subservience by his new boss, tyrannical land steward Phillip. The sudden news, to Jordan, that a million people died during the potato famine causes him to finally develop empathy, and it turns out to be a real pain.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: Strange things are afoot in Ballymacnoose: animals in small clothing, paranormal sightings of leprechauns, and most bizarrely of all, Callum gets his first ever match on a dating app. The one prickle on the pickle is that Gwen, Callum’s dream girl, is also in an open relationship with the 50-year-old Grainne, a woman who disembowels chickens for a living. Meanwhile, Gemma becomes obsessed with dressing farm animals in tiny clothing and causes Sammy to spin out in paranoia thinking that his farm has become infested with leprechauns. So Lorcan has no other choice but to introduce Gemma to the dark secrets of the Ballymacnoose Paranormal Society, also run by his da and Frank.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: Life in Ballymacnoose becomes very complicated when Callum accidentally walks in on Gemma and Lorcan trying out a new form of lovemaking. The sight triggers a long-buried childhood trauma in Callum and raises uncomfortable questions about the town’s deeply repressed relationship with sex. Can Ballymacnoose open its heart to true love? Meanwhile, Jordan has officially begun dating his much older lover, 50-year-old Grainne. But as their relationship deepens, Jordan is confronted with another harsh reality of adulthood: he’s going bald. Faced with the slow retreat of his hairline and the love of a good woman, Jordan must decide whether to cling to denial or embrace manhood in all its forms - love, responsibility and mushroom carbonaras.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: As Callum begins slowly unravelling under the strain of Jordan's relentless night terrors about baldness, he stumbles upon a flyer for Ballymacbot Wars - a local robot combat tournament offering a generous cash prize and potential ticket out of Jordan’s bedroom. Meanwhile, Jordan is uncharacteristically uninterested in the whole affair. He's become a bald hermit, terrified to leave the house and expose his creamy scalp to the outside world. That is, until, like a dagger in the night, a hooded burst of inspiration sends him back out into the world… and the robot wars.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: The gang belatedly get involved in the Great Famine, the one thing they didn’t need to get involved in. Callum’s new job at the Ballymac Folk Museum sends him down a spiral of method acting as a starving peasant. And he’s helped along in this grovelling subservience by his new boss, tyrannical land steward Phillip. The sudden news, to Jordan, that a million people died during the potato famine causes him to finally develop empathy, and it turns out to be a real pain.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: Strange things are afoot in Ballymacnoose: animals in small clothing, paranormal sightings of leprechauns, and most bizarrely of all, Callum gets his first ever match on a dating app. The one prickle on the pickle is that Gwen, Callum’s dream girl, is also in an open relationship with the 50-year-old Grainne, a woman who disembowels chickens for a living. Meanwhile, Gemma becomes obsessed with dressing farm animals in tiny clothing and causes Sammy to spin out in paranoia thinking that his farm has become infested with leprechauns. So Lorcan has no other choice but to introduce Gemma to the dark secrets of the Ballymacnoose Paranormal Society, also run by his da and Frank.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: Life in Ballymacnoose becomes very complicated when Callum accidentally walks in on Gemma and Lorcan trying out a new form of lovemaking. The sight triggers a long-buried childhood trauma in Callum and raises uncomfortable questions about the town’s deeply repressed relationship with sex. Can Ballymacnoose open its heart to true love? Meanwhile, Jordan has officially begun dating his much older lover, 50-year-old Grainne. But as their relationship deepens, Jordan is confronted with another harsh reality of adulthood: he’s going bald. Faced with the slow retreat of his hairline and the love of a good woman, Jordan must decide whether to cling to denial or embrace manhood in all its forms - love, responsibility and mushroom carbonaras.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: As Callum begins slowly unravelling under the strain of Jordan's relentless night terrors about baldness, he stumbles upon a flyer for Ballymacbot Wars - a local robot combat tournament offering a generous cash prize and potential ticket out of Jordan’s bedroom. Meanwhile, Jordan is uncharacteristically uninterested in the whole affair. He's become a bald hermit, terrified to leave the house and expose his creamy scalp to the outside world. That is, until, like a dagger in the night, a hooded burst of inspiration sends him back out into the world… and the robot wars.

programme.title: Pointless Celebrities
programme.desc: A special cricket edition of the general knowledge quiz in which four teams try to come up with the answers that no-one else could think of. Presented by Alexander Armstrong and co-host Richard Osman, with contestants Alison Mitchell, Andy Zaltzman, Devon Malcolm, Graham Gooch, Georgie Heath, Fran Wilson, Graeme Swann and Mark Ramprakash.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage as World Cup debutants Curacao play their second match in Group E against Ecuador at Kansas City Stadium. Curacao are the smallest nation ever to qualify for a World Cup and have the oldest coach in the tournament's history: 78-year-old former Rangers and Sunderland manager Dick Advocaat. Ecuador impressively finished second in South American qualifying and boast Chelsea midfielder Moises Caicedo in their ranks. It’s 20 years since their best performance at a World Cup, making the last 16 in 2006, when they were knocked out by England.

programme.title: Anna Haugh’s Big Irish Food Tour
programme.desc: When he's not touring the world, comedian Ed Byrne loves nothing more than to escape the bright lights for the splendour of the Wicklow mountains, Ireland's largest national park. Ed and Anna hike the Sally Gap, and he surprises her with a meal on the mountainside. After their feast, they search for sika deer in Glendalough with a local park ranger, learning about deer management. Anna also visits a sheep farming family known for their award-winning halloumi-style cheese.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: The gang belatedly get involved in the Great Famine, the one thing they didn’t need to get involved in. Callum’s new job at the Ballymac Folk Museum sends him down a spiral of method acting as a starving peasant. And he’s helped along in this grovelling subservience by his new boss, tyrannical land steward Phillip. The sudden news, to Jordan, that a million people died during the potato famine causes him to finally develop empathy, and it turns out to be a real pain.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: Strange things are afoot in Ballymacnoose: animals in small clothing, paranormal sightings of leprechauns, and most bizarrely of all, Callum gets his first ever match on a dating app. The one prickle on the pickle is that Gwen, Callum’s dream girl, is also in an open relationship with the 50-year-old Grainne, a woman who disembowels chickens for a living. Meanwhile, Gemma becomes obsessed with dressing farm animals in tiny clothing and causes Sammy to spin out in paranoia thinking that his farm has become infested with leprechauns. So Lorcan has no other choice but to introduce Gemma to the dark secrets of the Ballymacnoose Paranormal Society, also run by his da and Frank.

programme.title: Funboys

Meanwhile, Gemma becomes obsessed with dressing farm animals in tiny clothing and causes Sammy to spin out in paranoia thinking that his farm has become infested with leprechauns. So Lorcan has no other choice but to introduce Gemma to the dark secrets of the Ballymacnoose Paranormal Society, also run by his da and Frank.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: Life in Ballymacnoose becomes very complicated when Callum accidentally walks in on Gemma and Lorcan trying out a new form of lovemaking. The sight triggers a long-buried childhood trauma in Callum and raises uncomfortable questions about the town’s deeply repressed relationship with sex. Can Ballymacnoose open its heart to true love? Meanwhile, Jordan has officially begun dating his much older lover, 50-year-old Grainne. But as their relationship deepens, Jordan is confronted with another harsh reality of adulthood: he’s going bald. Faced with the slow retreat of his hairline and the love of a good woman, Jordan must decide whether to cling to denial or embrace manhood in all its forms - love, responsibility and mushroom carbonaras.

programme.title: Funboys

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: As Callum begins slowly unravelling under the strain of Jordan's relentless night terrors about baldness, he stumbles upon a flyer for Ballymacbot Wars - a local robot combat tournament offering a generous cash prize and potential ticket out of Jordan’s bedroom. Meanwhile, Jordan is uncharacteristically uninterested in the whole affair. He's become a bald hermit, terrified to leave the house and expose his creamy scalp to the outside world. That is, until, like a dagger in the night, a hooded burst of inspiration sends him back out into the world… and the robot wars.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage as World Cup debutants Curacao play their second match in Group E against Ecuador at Kansas City Stadium. Curacao are the smallest nation ever to qualify for a World Cup and have the oldest coach in the tournament's history: 78-year-old former Rangers and Sunderland manager Dick Advocaat. Ecuador impressively finished second in South American qualifying and boast Chelsea midfielder Moises Caicedo in their ranks. It’s 20 years since their best performance at a World Cup, making the last 16 in 2006, when they were knocked out by England.

programme.desc: Strange things are afoot in Ballymacnoose: animals in small clothing, paranormal sightings of leprechauns, and most bizarrely of all, Callum gets his first ever match on a dating app. The one prickle on the pickle is that Gwen, Callum’s dream girl, is also in an open relationship with the 50-year-old Grainne, a woman who disembowels chickens for a living. Meanwhile, Gemma becomes obsessed with dressing farm animals in tiny clothing and causes Sammy to spin out in paranoia thinking that his farm has become infested with leprechauns. So Lorcan has no other choice but to introduce Gemma to the dark secrets of the Ballymacnoose Paranormal Society, also run by his da and Frank.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: Life in Ballymacnoose becomes very complicated when Callum accidentally walks in on Gemma and Lorcan trying out a new form of lovemaking. The sight triggers a long-buried childhood trauma in Callum and raises uncomfortable questions about the town’s deeply repressed relationship with sex. Can Ballymacnoose open its heart to true love? Meanwhile, Jordan has officially begun dating his much older lover, 50-year-old Grainne. But as their relationship deepens, Jordan is confronted with another harsh reality of adulthood: he’s going bald. Faced with the slow retreat of his hairline and the love of a good woman, Jordan must decide whether to cling to denial or embrace manhood in all its forms - love, responsibility and mushroom carbonaras.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: As Callum begins slowly unravelling under the strain of Jordan's relentless night terrors about baldness, he stumbles upon a flyer for Ballymacbot Wars - a local robot combat tournament offering a generous cash prize and potential ticket out of Jordan’s bedroom. Meanwhile, Jordan is uncharacteristically uninterested in the whole affair. He's become a bald hermit, terrified to leave the house and expose his creamy scalp to the outside world. That is, until, like a dagger in the night, a hooded burst of inspiration sends him back out into the world… and the robot wars.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage as three-time World Cup finalists Netherlands stay in Texas for their second Group F game, this time in Houston against Sweden. This isn’t going to end well.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: The gang belatedly get involved in the Great Famine, the one thing they didn’t need to get involved in. Callum’s new job at the Ballymac Folk Museum sends him down a spiral of method acting as a starving peasant. And he’s helped along in this grovelling subservience by his new boss, tyrannical land steward Phillip. The sudden news, to Jordan, that a million people died during the potato famine causes him to finally develop empathy, and it turns out to be a real pain.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: Strange things are afoot in Ballymacnoose: animals in small clothing, paranormal sightings of leprechauns, and most bizarrely of all, Callum gets his first ever match on a dating app. The one prickle on the pickle is that Gwen, Callum’s dream girl, is also in an open relationship with the 50-year-old Grainne, a woman who disembowels chickens for a living. Meanwhile, Gemma becomes obsessed with dressing farm animals in tiny clothing and causes Sammy to spin out in paranoia thinking that his farm has become infested with leprechauns. So Lorcan has no other choice but to introduce Gemma to the dark secrets of the Ballymacnoose Paranormal Society, also run by his da and Frank.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: Life in Ballymacnoose becomes very complicated when Callum accidentally walks in on Gemma and Lorcan trying out a new form of lovemaking. The sight triggers a long-buried childhood trauma in Callum and raises uncomfortable questions about the town’s deeply repressed relationship with sex. Can Ballymacnoose open its heart to true love? Meanwhile, Jordan has officially begun dating his much older lover, 50-year-old Grainne. But as their relationship deepens, Jordan is confronted with another harsh reality of adulthood: he’s going bald. Faced with the slow retreat of his hairline and the love of a good woman, Jordan must decide whether to cling to denial or embrace manhood in all its forms - love, responsibility and mushroom carbonaras.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: As Callum begins slowly unravelling under the strain of Jordan's relentless night terrors about baldness, he stumbles upon a flyer for Ballymacbot Wars - a local robot combat tournament offering a generous cash prize and potential ticket out of Jordan’s bedroom. Meanwhile, Jordan is uncharacteristically uninterested in the whole affair. He's become a bald hermit, terrified to leave the house and expose his creamy scalp to the outside world. That is, until, like a dagger in the night, a hooded burst of inspiration sends him back out into the world… and the robot wars.

programme.title: Pointless Celebrities
programme.desc: A special cricket edition of the general knowledge quiz in which four teams try to come up with the answers that no-one else could think of. Presented by Alexander Armstrong and co-host Richard Osman, with contestants Alison Mitchell, Andy Zaltzman, Devon Malcolm, Graham Gooch, Georgie Heath, Fran Wilson, Graeme Swann and Mark Ramprakash.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage as World Cup debutants Curacao play their second match in Group E against Ecuador at Kansas City Stadium. Curacao are the smallest nation ever to qualify for a World Cup and have the oldest coach in the tournament's history: 78-year-old former Rangers and Sunderland manager Dick Advocaat. Ecuador impressively finished second in South American qualifying and boast Chelsea midfielder Moises Caicedo in their ranks. It’s 20 years since their best performance at a World Cup, making the last 16 in 2006, when they were knocked out by England.

Faced with the slow retreat of his hairline and the love of a good woman, Jordan must decide whether to cling to denial or embrace manhood in all its forms - love, responsibility and mushroom carbonaras.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: As Callum begins slowly unravelling under the strain of Jordan's relentless night terrors about baldness, he stumbles upon a flyer for Ballymacbot Wars - a local robot combat tournament offering a generous cash prize and potential ticket out of Jordan’s bedroom. programme.title: Funboys

programme.title: Schitt's Creek
programme.desc: Johnny and Moira come to a shocking realisation that they might be terrible parents. They attempt to get to know their twenty-something children, but David and Alexis avoid their parents' intrusive interest, with David trying to sell some of his clothes for extra cash and Alexis investigating Mutt’s mysterious relationship with the mayor’s wife. Johnny and Moira speak with Roland and Jocelyn about parenting and realise that all parents have issues with their children.

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: Agnes Brown has family troubles to contend with: her son Dermot has fallen out with Maria Nicholson, his long-term girlfriend, and Grandad is feeling poorly. After a sleepless night, Mrs Brown decides to try to sort out Dermot and Maria's problem by giving Maria the benefit of her advice. But her heart-to-heart with Maria only succeeds in making the dispute worse. So Mrs Brown's daughter Cathy intervenes. She's a psychology student, and offers Dermot and Maria a counselling session. A dismayed Mrs Brown can't help interfering, and the session quickly descends into a blazing row between her and Cathy... with an effect on Dermot and Maria that not even Agnes Brown could have predicted. Meanwhile, Grandad ends up in hospital when Dr Flynn's attempt to read his temperature goes dramatically wrong. And Cathy reveals the electrifying secret of how she keeps dodgy men at bay.

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: Agnes Brown is concerned that her family are keeping too many secrets. Her daughter Cathy won't let her meet her new boyfriend. Her elder son Mark won't reveal why his feisty wife Betty has thrown him out. And her younger son Dermot has lied to his fiancee Maria Nicholson's well-to-do parents about the status of his job. When Betty and Mrs Brown meet to discuss Mark's problem, they unsurprisingly come to blows. Unfortunately their row happens in front of Dermot's posh future mother-in-law Mrs Nicholson, who has come round to discuss arrangements for her daughter's wedding. Horrified by what she witnesses, Mrs Nicholson decides that the Brown family are so rough she will try to stop them attending the wedding. Then Mrs Brown spots Betty with another man, and concludes that Betty and Mark have fallen out because Betty is having an affair. But when she finally confronts Betty, Agnes is confounded to discover that Mark is the one who has something to hide: a guilty secret for which Agnes has only herself to blame.

programme.title: Two Pints of Lager and a Packet of Crisps
programme.desc: Janet is keen to improve her mind but realises that neither poetry nor biscuits are the answer. Gaz is desperate to feel attractive and thinks that the best way to accomplish this is to flash his rather underdeveloped chest.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: The gang belatedly get involved in the Great Famine, the one thing they didn’t need to get involved in. Callum’s new job at the Ballymac Folk Museum sends him down a spiral of method acting as a starving peasant. And he’s helped along in this grovelling subservience by his new boss, tyrannical land steward Phillip. The sudden news, to Jordan, that a million people died during the potato famine causes him to finally develop empathy, and it turns out to be a real pain.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: Strange things are afoot in Ballymacnoose: animals in small clothing, paranormal sightings of leprechauns, and most bizarrely of all, Callum gets his first ever match on a dating app. The one prickle on the pickle is that Gwen, Callum’s dream girl, is also in an open relationship with the 50-year-old Grainne, a woman who disembowels chickens for a living. Meanwhile, Gemma becomes obsessed with dressing farm animals in tiny clothing and causes Sammy to spin out in paranoia thinking that his farm has become infested with leprechauns. So Lorcan has no other choice but to introduce Gemma to the dark secrets of the Ballymacnoose Paranormal Society, also run by his da and Frank.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: Life in Ballymacnoose becomes very complicated when Callum accidentally walks in on Gemma and Lorcan trying out a new form of lovemaking. The sight triggers a long-buried childhood trauma in Callum and raises uncomfortable questions about the town’s deeply repressed relationship with sex. Can Ballymacnoose open its heart to true love? Meanwhile, Jordan has officially begun dating his much older lover, 50-year-old Grainne. But as their relationship deepens, Jordan is confronted with another harsh reality of adulthood: he’s going bald. Faced with the slow retreat of his hairline and the love of a good woman, Jordan must decide whether to cling to denial or embrace manhood in all its forms - love, responsibility and mushroom carbonaras.

programme.title: The Young Offenders
programme.desc: Facing a dilemma, Siobhan makes a plan with Linda to meet the lads on a bus. An unexpected intervention by local bully Billy Murphy leads to an accidental wild bus ride around Cork, ultimately bringing everyone closer together.

programme.title: Ideal
programme.desc: Manchester-based comedy series starring Johnny Vegas as small-time dope dealer Moz. His girlfriend moves out when a rat appears in his flat, then menacing rival dealer Psycho Paul has a score to settle.

programme.title: Ideal
programme.desc: Manchester-based comedy series starring Johnny Vegas as small-time dope dealer Moz. While his girlfriend is away, Moz tries to seduce the beautiful China, but his plans are interrupted by another appearance from the rat.

programme.title: Ideal
programme.desc: Manchester-based comedy series starring Johnny Vegas as small-time dope dealer Moz. Moz learns about a local murder, meets his stalker and makes up with Nicki. Meanwhile, China's new boyfriend Cartoon Head has something to hide.

programme.title: Ideal
programme.desc: Manchester-based comedy starring Johnny Vegas as small-time dope dealer Moz. Moz gives a local band a hand and the police help him shake off his stalker. After China splits with Cartoon Head, Moz is keen to provide a shoulder to cry on.

programme.title: BBC Comedy Short Films
programme.desc: It’s the first day of sixth form, and Mike is looking forward to a bit of social mobility. He thinks he’s way better than the group of so-called 'loser' friends he’s somehow accrued, and aspires to higher things. But for now, he’s stuck with powergeek Sonny and Dan, a lad who only communicates in put-downs, and he’s going to find it hard to shake them off: Mike, Sonny and Dan all take the mobility bus to school. Mike has cerebral palsy, Sonny uses a wheelchair, and Dan ‘Syndrome’ Simmons has Down’s Syndrome. So Mike, Sonny and Dan are trapped together – at least for the ride to school.

programme.title: Doctor Who (2005–2022)
programme.desc: The Doctor and Clara face their last Christmas. Trapped on an Arctic base, under attack from terrifying creatures, who are you going to call? Santa Claus!

programme.title: Miranda
programme.desc: Miranda has decided to prove to herself and her friends that she can officially be an adult. She starts by looking after a toddler, but the soft play centre is too much of a lure and she gets stuck in a kids' tunnel. She then hosts a dinner party for eight, which ends in inevitable chaos.

programme.title: Miranda
programme.desc: Miranda has been caring for her ill mother for five very long days. Trapped in her flat and being barked at by Penny, she is forced to think about her life regrets. Before she has the chance to tick off her bucket list she gets ill, and Tilly, Gary and Stevie offer no sympathy or help at all.

programme.title: Schitt's Creek
programme.desc: The Rose family's lives are changed forever when the government comes to collect years of back taxes. Left with almost nothing, they must move to Johnny’s last remaining asset, Schitt’s Creek. When Johnny offends the town’s mayor, Roland Schitt, the Rose family soon discovers that the doors to their motel rooms have been taken. It’s now up to Johnny to set things right in the hope that his family can sleep safely on their first night in their new home.

programme.title: Schitt's Creek
programme.desc: After Johnny awakes soaking wet from a leaking pipe in the ceiling, he decides that he must sell the town, but soon discovers that this is easier said than done. He needs to get Roland’s approval before he can put the town on the market. Meanwhile, the Rose children check out the local nightlife by attending a tailgate party. Alexis uses the opportunity to scope for a new boyfriend, while David gets to know Stevie, the girl that runs the motel.

programme.title: Schitt's Creek
programme.desc: Johnny is shocked to see the pornographic-looking town sign and plans to get it taken down. When he talks to the town council about it, he finds out that the sign is very important to Roland for family reasons. Meanwhile, David is faced with the near-impossible task of finding a job, while Alexis starts her community service and is paired with Mutt, the guy she kissed the night before.

programme.title: Reported Missing
programme.desc: Police concerns grow about the mental state of two missing teens - 16-year-old Larissa has disappeared after an argument with her mum, and 18-year-old Bobby may be a suicide risk.

programme.title: Gareth Southgate: Changing the Game for Young Men
programme.desc: Former England men's football manager Gareth Southgate reveals the struggles many boys and young men face, asking why some feel left behind and what could help them move forward.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: In May last year, three arson attacks targeted the prime minister, Keir Starmer. Two properties and a car were set alight. But who lit the fires and why? Daniel De Simone investigates and finds the shadowy figures behind the attacks were also behind fake far-right groups trying to stoke hatred and division in the UK. The fires fit a pattern in which hostile states such as Russia are increasingly using proxies here to do their dirty work. So could Russia be behind the Starmer fires?

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: Out in the ocean, the Piripenguins encounter a massive, angry whale called Norman, who wrecks their boat. Can the Piripenguins brave their fears and find a way to cheer him up?

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: Dad needs some training to pass his astronaut fitness test. Cosima and Big Lizard put him through his paces! When Rex gets into trouble, Dad’s hard work finally pays off.

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: The ducklings look after the sheep while wearing cowboy hats and riding a hen. This gives Weasy the idea to have a rodeo session with one of the sheep - but it won't buck! The ducklings must stop their father from upsetting the animals.

programme.title: Super Happy Magic Forest
programme.desc: While questing to keep her hero safe on her long journey, superfan Blossom fusses and frets too much, making things awkward.

programme.title: Grizzy and the Lemmings
programme.desc: It's time for the racket game, where big scores mean big prizes.

programme.title: Duck and Frog
programme.desc: When looking after their neighbours' baby, Duck soon learns that he is a terrible babysitter - though it seems kids love Frog! Duck needs Frog to help out for once but soon loses the baby.

programme.title: Pokémon Horizons
programme.desc: Liko, Roy and Ult reunite with Dot and Murdock in Cortondo.

programme.title: Bro's in Control
programme.desc: Adam and Joe race across Lapland to deliver Callum’s letter to Santa before putting their elf skills to the test in the ultimate Christmas challenge!

programme.title: Gladiators: Epic Pranks
programme.desc: Nitro, Fire, Hammer and Apollo go head-to-head to rack up prank points - but will ponytails, air guitars, inflatable flamingos or zebras lead to a tap-out?

programme.title: Blue Peter
programme.desc: Hacker meets the stars of Toy Story 5, while Abby takes two superfans behind the scenes of West End production My Neighbour Totoro, with exclusive access to the magical puppets which bring the story to life. Also, Queen of the Jungle, Scarlett Moffatt, joins us in the studio!

programme.title: Newsround
programme.desc: Topical news magazine for children.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: A special programme from Birmingham in the heart of Gardeners’ World Live – an annual vibrant celebration of practical gardening and bold design. Monty Don is joined by Frances Tophill, Adam Frost, Arit Anderson and Sue Kent for an hour packed with ideas, inspiration and expert advice. The team explore standout gardens, meet the people shaping the future of horticulture and reveal practical takeaways viewers can try at home. Sustainability is in the spotlight as pioneering growers reveal why cork could be a game-changing material – and how it’s already transforming the way they garden. There’s a surprising and ambitious show garden co-designed by Professor Alice Roberts, bringing the story of evolution to life through plants, and a first-time designer whose passion for railways has inspired a unique garden guaranteed to turn heads.

programme.title: My Darling Clementine
programme.desc: Marshal Wyatt Earp tries to clean up the lawless town of Tombstone with the help of his brothers and gambler Doc Holliday. But trouble with the Clanton Gang leads to the legendary 'gunfight at the OK Corral'.

programme.title: She Wore a Yellow Ribbon
programme.desc: In the second in John Ford's cavalry trilogy, a US cavalry officer suffers a setback on his last mission and is 'retired' before he can take further action. To avert a full-scale war, he decides to act alone.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martel heads to Shildon in County Durham to see a two-bed mid-terrace bought by an enthusiastic first-time developer. Dion visits a rather unusual lot in Derby that has great potential for transformation. Jacqui is in Seaford, East Sussex, to see a former care home that is also a great opportunity for a developer with the right skills.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: It’s all go in gorgeous Powys as Jules Hudson helps a couple to swap town life in Oxfordshire for his beloved Wales. On the wish list is space for two dogs, three cats and a garage for a motorbike, which the brand spanking new mystery eco-house might just deliver. For an inspiring change of pace, Jules visits a brilliant local farming initiative that’s helping young people get into agriculture and grow sustainable food for the future.

programme.title: Battle of Britain
programme.desc: 1940. Britain fears an impending German invasion. Goering is confident his Luftwaffe will pave the way for success. It falls to brave squadrons of fighter pilots to fend off the attack from the air.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin revisits some of the locations visited by Flog It! and presents all-new valuations. Experts touch down at Bletchley Park, the Ulster Transport Museum and Crowcombe Court to track down some unusual items to sell at auction. They uncover a beautiful watercolour and some stunning porcelain, and Paul Martin visits Antony in Cornwall to unearth a fascinating family history.

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: Two top TV journalists, former BBC royal correspondent Jennie Bond and newsreader Simon McCoy, take up the antiques challenge and go rummaging all around Devon. The two, who became firm friends whilst reporting on some quite tumultuous times, now find themselves chasing scoops once again. With £400 each and experts Margie Cooper and Raj Bisram along to help, Jennie and Simon will be piloting through the B-roads of Devon in an Austin Healey and an E-Type Jaguar.

programme.title: Grand Tours of Scotland's Lochs
programme.desc: Paul Murton’s loch-hopping journey across Scotland reaches the quiet lochs of the Borders, where he learns dog-handling techniques at a school for sheepdogs and then heads to some man-made lochs in the Moorfoot Hills, where he hears tell of hidden treasure. In Edinburgh, he discovers the story of a Dutch-speaking Scottish minister on skates and goes in search of a lost river and two long-vanished lochs in the heart of the city. Crossing the Firth of Forth, Paul travels around the industrial lochs of the old Fife coal field, before walking in the footsteps of Mary, Queen of Scots on a haunted island in Loch Leven.

programme.title: Cricket: Today at the Test
programme.desc: Day 4 highlights from the second Test match between England and New Zealand.

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: Midge Ure looks back at the 1986 Prince’s Trust Rock Concert, organised to celebrate the tenth anniversary of the charity. As musical director for the event, he is perfectly placed to discuss a show that included stars such as Tina Turner, Eric Clapton, Phil Collins and Elton John. He describes how the concert was rehearsed, how worried he was about getting songs wrong, his favourite moments and the joyous spontaneity of seeing acts perform that would never been seen together at any other time or place.

programme.title: The Prince's Trust Rock Gala 1986
programme.desc: On 20 June 1986, to celebrate the tenth anniversary of the Prince's Trust, a concert of superstars from the world of pop music performed for the Prince and Princess of Wales. The birthday concert took place at Wembley Arena in London and featured Big Country, Level 42, Suzanne Vega and, for the one night only, the supergroup Birthday Party, including Phil Collins, Midge Ure, Mark Knopfler, Rod Stewart, Elton John, Eric Clapton, Joan Armatrading, Howard Jones, Paul Young, Tina Turner and special guests.

programme.title: Tina Turner: Wildest Dreams Live in Amsterdam 1996
programme.desc: Tina Turner lifted the roof off the new Amsterdam Arena for three sizzling nights in September 1996, in front of 150,000 people, as part of her record-breaking Wildest Dreams European tour, on which she performed over 150 shows to over 3,000,000 people. Performing many of the hits which have made her famous, this concert captures the spirit of those nights. Songs include River Deep Mountain High, Nutbush City Limits, GoldenEye, The Best, Steamy Windows, Missing You, In Your Wildest Dreams, We Don’t Need Another Hero, Private Dancer and What’s Love Got to Do with It.

programme.title: TRNSMT
programme.desc: Shereen Cutkelvin presents highlights of the second day of TRNSMT from Glasgow Green, featuring The Last Dinner Party, The Snuts, Sonny Fodera, Brogeal, The Fratellis, Rianne Downey, Loyle Carner and Kasabian.

Performing many of the hits which have made her famous, this concert captures the spirit of those nights. Songs include River Deep Mountain High, Nutbush City Limits, GoldenEye, The Best, Steamy Windows, Missing You, In Your Wildest Dreams, We Don’t Need Another Hero, Private Dancer and What’s Love Got to Do with It.

programme.title: TRNSMT
programme.desc: Shereen Cutkelvin presents highlights of the second day of TRNSMT from Glasgow Green, featuring The Last Dinner Party, The Snuts, Sonny Fodera, Brogeal, The Fratellis, Rianne Downey, Loyle Carner and Kasabian.

programme.title: Reported Missing
programme.desc: Police concerns grow about the mental state of two missing teens - 16-year-old Larissa has disappeared after an argument with her mum, and 18-year-old Bobby may be a suicide risk.

programme.title: Gareth Southgate: Changing the Game for Young Men
programme.desc: Former England men's football manager Gareth Southgate reveals the struggles many boys and young men face, asking why some feel left behind and what could help them move forward.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: In May last year, three arson attacks targeted the prime minister, Keir Starmer. Two properties and a car were set alight. But who lit the fires and why? Daniel De Simone investigates and finds the shadowy figures behind the attacks were also behind fake far-right groups trying to stoke hatred and division in the UK. The fires fit a pattern in which hostile states such as Russia are increasingly using proxies here to do their dirty work. So could Russia be behind the Starmer fires?

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: Out in the ocean, the Piripenguins encounter a massive, angry whale called Norman, who wrecks their boat. Can the Piripenguins brave their fears and find a way to cheer him up?

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: Dad needs some training to pass his astronaut fitness test. Cosima and Big Lizard put him through his paces! When Rex gets into trouble, Dad’s hard work finally pays off.

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: The ducklings look after the sheep while wearing cowboy hats and riding a hen. This gives Weasy the idea to have a rodeo session with one of the sheep - but it won't buck! The ducklings must stop their father from upsetting the animals.

programme.title: Super Happy Magic Forest
programme.desc: While questing to keep her hero safe on her long journey, superfan Blossom fusses and frets too much, making things awkward.

programme.title: Grizzy and the Lemmings
programme.desc: It's time for the racket game, where big scores mean big prizes.

programme.title: Duck and Frog
programme.desc: When looking after their neighbours' baby, Duck soon learns that he is a terrible babysitter - though it seems kids love Frog! Duck needs Frog to help out for once but soon loses the baby.

programme.title: Pokémon Horizons
programme.desc: Liko, Roy and Ult reunite with Dot and Murdock in Cortondo.

programme.title: Bro's in Control
programme.desc: Adam and Joe race across Lapland to deliver Callum’s letter to Santa before putting their elf skills to the test in the ultimate Christmas challenge!

programme.title: Gladiators: Epic Pranks
programme.desc: Nitro, Fire, Hammer and Apollo go head-to-head to rack up prank points - but will ponytails, air guitars, inflatable flamingos or zebras lead to a tap-out?

programme.title: Blue Peter
programme.desc: Hacker meets the stars of Toy Story 5, while Abby takes two superfans behind the scenes of West End production My Neighbour Totoro, with exclusive access to the magical puppets which bring the story to life. Also, Queen of the Jungle, Scarlett Moffatt, joins us in the studio!

programme.title: Newsround
programme.desc: Topical news magazine for children.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: A special programme from Birmingham in the heart of Gardeners’ World Live – an annual vibrant celebration of practical gardening and bold design. Monty Don is joined by Frances Tophill, Adam Frost, Arit Anderson and Sue Kent for an hour packed with ideas, inspiration and expert advice. The team explore standout gardens, meet the people shaping the future of horticulture and reveal practical takeaways viewers can try at home. Sustainability is in the spotlight as pioneering growers reveal why cork could be a game-changing material – and how it’s already transforming the way they garden. There’s a surprising and ambitious show garden co-designed by Professor Alice Roberts, bringing the story of evolution to life through plants, and a first-time designer whose passion for railways has inspired a unique garden guaranteed to turn heads.

programme.title: My Darling Clementine
programme.desc: Marshal Wyatt Earp tries to clean up the lawless town of Tombstone with the help of his brothers and gambler Doc Holliday. But trouble with the Clanton Gang leads to the legendary 'gunfight at the OK Corral'.

programme.title: She Wore a Yellow Ribbon
programme.desc: In the second in John Ford's cavalry trilogy, a US cavalry officer suffers a setback on his last mission and is 'retired' before he can take further action. To avert a full-scale war, he decides to act alone.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martel heads to Shildon in County Durham to see a two-bed mid-terrace bought by an enthusiastic first-time developer. Dion visits a rather unusual lot in Derby that has great potential for transformation. Jacqui is in Seaford, East Sussex, to see a former care home that is also a great opportunity for a developer with the right skills.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: It’s all go in gorgeous Powys as Jules Hudson helps a couple to swap town life in Oxfordshire for his beloved Wales. On the wish list is space for two dogs, three cats and a garage for a motorbike, which the brand spanking new mystery eco-house might just deliver. For an inspiring change of pace, Jules visits a brilliant local farming initiative that’s helping young people get into agriculture and grow sustainable food for the future.

programme.title: Battle of Britain
programme.desc: 1940. Britain fears an impending German invasion. Goering is confident his Luftwaffe will pave the way for success. It falls to brave squadrons of fighter pilots to fend off the attack from the air.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin revisits some of the locations visited by Flog It! and presents all-new valuations. Experts touch down at Bletchley Park, the Ulster Transport Museum and Crowcombe Court to track down some unusual items to sell at auction. They uncover a beautiful watercolour and some stunning porcelain, and Paul Martin visits Antony in Cornwall to unearth a fascinating family history.

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: Two top TV journalists, former BBC royal correspondent Jennie Bond and newsreader Simon McCoy, take up the antiques challenge and go rummaging all around Devon. The two, who became firm friends whilst reporting on some quite tumultuous times, now find themselves chasing scoops once again. With £400 each and experts Margie Cooper and Raj Bisram along to help, Jennie and Simon will be piloting through the B-roads of Devon in an Austin Healey and an E-Type Jaguar.

programme.title: Grand Tours of Scotland's Lochs
programme.desc: Paul Murton’s loch-hopping journey across Scotland reaches the quiet lochs of the Borders, where he learns dog-handling techniques at a school for sheepdogs and then heads to some man-made lochs in the Moorfoot Hills, where he hears tell of hidden treasure. In Edinburgh, he discovers the story of a Dutch-speaking Scottish minister on skates and goes in search of a lost river and two long-vanished lochs in the heart of the city. Crossing the Firth of Forth, Paul travels around the industrial lochs of the old Fife coal field, before walking in the footsteps of Mary, Queen of Scots on a haunted island in Loch Leven.

programme.title: Cricket: Today at the Test
programme.desc: Day 4 highlights from the second Test match between England and New Zealand.

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: Midge Ure looks back at the 1986 Prince’s Trust Rock Concert, organised to celebrate the tenth anniversary of the charity. As musical director for the event, he is perfectly placed to discuss a show that included stars such as Tina Turner, Eric Clapton, Phil Collins and Elton John. He describes how the concert was rehearsed, how worried he was about getting songs wrong, his favourite moments and the joyous spontaneity of seeing acts perform that would never been seen together at any other time or place.

programme.title: The Prince's Trust Rock Gala 1986
programme.desc: On 20 June 1986, to celebrate the tenth anniversary of the Prince's Trust, a concert of superstars from the world of pop music performed for the Prince and Princess of Wales. The birthday concert took place at Wembley Arena in London and featured Big Country, Level 42, Suzanne Vega and, for the one night only, the supergroup Birthday Party, including Phil Collins, Midge Ure, Mark Knopfler, Rod Stewart, Elton John, Eric Clapton, Joan Armatrading, Howard Jones, Paul Young, Tina Turner and special guests.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek Brockway is in Pembrokeshire with its majestic cliffs, feeling what it is like to be exposed to the elements. He is thrilled to peek at seal pups along the way, learns how to train a sheepdog, builds a stone wall and helps to create a unique sand circle.

programme.title: The Hairy Bikers' Cookbook
programme.desc: From birthday cakes to traditional wedding cakes, Simon King and Dave Myers delve into the world of celebration cakes and face their biggest challenge to date - making a five-tier wedding cake. The Hairies journey to Manchester to meet Helen and Jonnie, the couple who are prepared to let them loose on their wedding cake. The boys decide to bake a traditional fruit cake with a Hairy Bikers twist, using quantities of ingredients so large the cake has to be mixed in a wheelbarrow. After baking and marzipanning the cakes, the boys attend sugar craft lessons before they attempt to begin decorating and then constructing the five tiers. It is art meets engineering for the boys, and the bride and groom are followed in the nail-biting lead-up to their wedding.

programme.title: Springwatch in Wales
programme.desc: Iolo Williams recalls the best marine stories from the seas off Wales. A young tropical turtle stranded in north Wales needs dedicated care from Anglesey Sea Zoo, while Chris Packham reveals the delicate and curious lives of moon jellyfish. Iolo recalls his own visit to help the gannets of Grassholm Island with the challenges of plastic and more recently bird flu, but black-eyed flu survivors are helping the colony begin a slow fight back. Gillian Burke joins a sea mammal survey and takes a closer look at the bottlenose dolphins of Cardigan Bay, while Iolo reports a new sighting of a minke whale there, too - the first in ten years.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: A special programme from Birmingham in the heart of Gardeners’ World Live – an annual vibrant celebration of practical gardening and bold design. Monty Don is joined by Frances Tophill, Adam Frost, Arit Anderson and Sue Kent for an hour packed with ideas, inspiration and expert advice. The team explore standout gardens, meet the people shaping the future of horticulture and reveal practical takeaways viewers can try at home. Sustainability is in the spotlight as pioneering growers reveal why cork could be a game-changing material – and how it’s already transforming the way they garden. There’s a surprising and ambitious show garden co-designed by Professor Alice Roberts, bringing the story of evolution to life through plants, and a first-time designer whose passion for railways has inspired a unique garden guaranteed to turn heads.

programme.title: My Darling Clementine
programme.desc: Marshal Wyatt Earp tries to clean up the lawless town of Tombstone with the help of his brothers and gambler Doc Holliday. But trouble with the Clanton Gang leads to the legendary 'gunfight at the OK Corral'.

programme.title: She Wore a Yellow Ribbon
programme.desc: In the second in John Ford's cavalry trilogy, a US cavalry officer suffers a setback on his last mission and is 'retired' before he can take further action. To avert a full-scale war, he decides to act alone.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martel heads to Shildon in County Durham to see a two-bed mid-terrace bought by an enthusiastic first-time developer. Dion visits a rather unusual lot in Derby that has great potential for transformation. Jacqui is in Seaford, East Sussex, to see a former care home that is also a great opportunity for a developer with the right skills.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek Brockway is in Pembrokeshire with its majestic cliffs, feeling what it is like to be exposed to the elements. He is thrilled to peek at seal pups along the way, learns how to train a sheepdog, builds a stone wall and helps to create a unique sand circle.

programme.title: The Hairy Bikers' Cookbook
programme.desc: From birthday cakes to traditional wedding cakes, Simon King and Dave Myers delve into the world of celebration cakes and face their biggest challenge to date - making a five-tier wedding cake. The Hairies journey to Manchester to meet Helen and Jonnie, the couple who are prepared to let them loose on their wedding cake. The boys decide to bake a traditional fruit cake with a Hairy Bikers twist, using quantities of ingredients so large the cake has to be mixed in a wheelbarrow. After baking and marzipanning the cakes, the boys attend sugar craft lessons before they attempt to begin decorating and then constructing the five tiers. It is art meets engineering for the boys, and the bride and groom are followed in the nail-biting lead-up to their wedding.

programme.title: Battle of Britain
programme.desc: 1940. Britain fears an impending German invasion. Goering is confident his Luftwaffe will pave the way for success. It falls to brave squadrons of fighter pilots to fend off the attack from the air.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin revisits some of the locations visited by Flog It! and presents all-new valuations. Experts touch down at Bletchley Park, the Ulster Transport Museum and Crowcombe Court to track down some unusual items to sell at auction. They uncover a beautiful watercolour and some stunning porcelain, and Paul Martin visits Antony in Cornwall to unearth a fascinating family history.

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: Two top TV journalists, former BBC royal correspondent Jennie Bond and newsreader Simon McCoy, take up the antiques challenge and go rummaging all around Devon. The two, who became firm friends whilst reporting on some quite tumultuous times, now find themselves chasing scoops once again. With £400 each and experts Margie Cooper and Raj Bisram along to help, Jennie and Simon will be piloting through the B-roads of Devon in an Austin Healey and an E-Type Jaguar.

programme.title: Springwatch in Wales
programme.desc: Iolo Williams recalls the best marine stories from the seas off Wales. A young tropical turtle stranded in north Wales needs dedicated care from Anglesey Sea Zoo, while Chris Packham reveals the delicate and curious lives of moon jellyfish. Iolo recalls his own visit to help the gannets of Grassholm Island with the challenges of plastic and more recently bird flu, but black-eyed flu survivors are helping the colony begin a slow fight back. Gillian Burke joins a sea mammal survey and takes a closer look at the bottlenose dolphins of Cardigan Bay, while Iolo reports a new sighting of a minke whale there, too - the first in ten years.

programme.title: Cricket: Today at the Test

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: Midge Ure looks back at the 1986 Prince’s Trust Rock Concert, organised to celebrate the tenth anniversary of the charity. As musical director for the event, he is perfectly placed to discuss a show that included stars such as Tina Turner, Eric Clapton, Phil Collins and Elton John. He describes how the concert was rehearsed, how worried he was about getting songs wrong, his favourite moments and the joyous spontaneity of seeing acts perform that would never been seen together at any other time or place.

programme.title: The Prince's Trust Rock Gala 1986
programme.desc: On 20 June 1986, to celebrate the tenth anniversary of the Prince's Trust, a concert of superstars from the world of pop music performed for the Prince and Princess of Wales. The birthday concert took place at Wembley Arena in London and featured Big Country, Level 42, Suzanne Vega and, for the one night only, the supergroup Birthday Party, including Phil Collins, Midge Ure, Mark Knopfler, Rod Stewart, Elton John, Eric Clapton, Joan Armatrading, Howard Jones, Paul Young, Tina Turner and special guests.

programme.title: Tina Turner: Wildest Dreams Live in Amsterdam 1996
programme.desc: Tina Turner lifted the roof off the new Amsterdam Arena for three sizzling nights in September 1996, in front of 150,000 people, as part of her record-breaking Wildest Dreams European tour, on which she performed over 150 shows to over 3,000,000 people. Performing many of the hits which have made her famous, this concert captures the spirit of those nights. Songs include River Deep Mountain High, Nutbush City Limits, GoldenEye, The Best, Steamy Windows, Missing You, In Your Wildest Dreams, We Don’t Need Another Hero, Private Dancer and What’s Love Got to Do with It.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: James and his travelling companion Nick Nairn continue their Scottish adventure in Lossiemouth, which is home to the first RAF squadron and a fleet of Typhoon fighter jets - James fulfils a lifetime ambition of training in a Typhoon flight simulator before heading airside to cook up homemade crumpets with buttered lobster, spinach and samphire for the RAF staff. James next pays a visit to two ex-RAF Lossiemouth pilots who are living the dream and running their own craft brewery just down the road from their old base - he's so inspired that he takes some of their beer and uses it to make a classic comforting one-pot beef stew and dumplings. Back at Lossiemouth, Nick shows the base's young recruits some tasty recipe suggestions that they can make in their digs, and there's a surprise in store as James has arranged for him to be put through his paces at an RAF fitness test. Finally, James takes one of the area's most abundant fish and makes mackerel and cauliflower with mango dressing.

programme.title: Love Your Garden
programme.desc: Alan Titchmarsh, David Domoney and Danny Clarke transform a small Leicester garden into a Caribbean-inspired technicolour paradise. Showing how colour can reinvigorate size or shape of garden, Alan and the boys' challenge is to create the perfect space for community worker Jules Richards, inspired by her love of Barbados. Meanwhile, in a separate garden Frances Tophill reveals how to use light coloured landscaping, shade-loving flowers and sculpture to bring beauty and vibrancy to a dark corner.

programme.title: Ainsley's Fantastic Flavours
programme.desc: Knocking up some tempting treats - and not just desserts - Ainsley makes some incredible dishes with a sweet twist! Caramelised, glazed and iced, perfect for those of us with a real sweet tooth, Ainsley makes Korean-inspired pork skewers and an American favourite with spicy and sweet buffalo sauce. Paralympic swimmer Ellie Simmonds pops in to show us how to make her family recipe for chocolate cheesecake, and Ainsley samples another Maltese classic.

programme.desc: National and international news with reports and analysis from ITV's Correspondents in the UK and around the world. [S]

programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: In Donegal Town, Dermot's journey takes him further south along the Wild Atlantic Way, discovering a place where Irish tradition and global flavours sit side by side. His day begins at family-run Hannah Hats, where he's fitted in iconic Donegal tweed and learns why this rugged corner of Ireland became famous for its beautifully flecked fabric. Dressed fit for a fine meal, Dermot visits one of Ireland's most unexpected culinary hotspots: Chandpur, widely regarded as Ireland's best curry house. He meets Bangladeshi-born chef Rana, and together they cook railway curry using outstanding local Donegal lamb and potatoes - it's a heaven-made match of Asian flavours and quality Irish produce. For pudding, Dermot meets chef Brian McDermott, one of the biggest champions of Donegal's food scene. Together they bake a classic Irish apple pie, with Brian revealing why all the local rain creates richer grass, creamier milk and extra buttery pastry, making Donegal Town a dessert destination.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure

James next pays a visit to two ex-RAF Lossiemouth pilots who are living the dream and running their own craft brewery just down the road from their old base - he's so inspired that he takes some of their beer and uses it to make a classic comforting one-pot beef stew and dumplings. Finally, James takes one of the area's most abundant fish and makes mackerel and cauliflower with mango dressing.

His day begins at family-run Hannah Hats, where he's fitted in iconic Donegal tweed and learns why this rugged corner of Ireland became famous for its beautifully flecked fabric. Dressed fit for a fine meal, Dermot visits one of Ireland's most unexpected culinary hotspots: Chandpur, widely regarded as Ireland's best curry house. He meets Bangladeshi-born chef Rana, and together they cook railway curry using outstanding local Donegal lamb and potatoes - it's a heaven-made match of Asian flavours and quality Irish produce. For pudding, Dermot meets chef Brian McDermott, one of the biggest champions of Donegal's food scene. Together they bake a classic Irish apple pie, with Brian revealing why all the local rain creates richer grass, creamier milk and extra buttery pastry, making Donegal Town a dessert destination.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: James and his travelling companion Nick Nairn continue their Scottish adventure in Lossiemouth, which is home to the first RAF squadron and a fleet of Typhoon fighter jets - James fulfils a lifetime ambition of training in a Typhoon flight simulator before heading airside to cook up homemade crumpets with buttered lobster, spinach and samphire for the RAF staff. James next pays a visit to two ex-RAF Lossiemouth pilots who are living the dream and running their own craft brewery just down the road from their old base - he's so inspired that he takes some of their beer and uses it to make a classic comforting one-pot beef stew and dumplings. Back at Lossiemouth, Nick shows the base's young recruits some tasty recipe suggestions that they can make in their digs, and there's a surprise in store as James has arranged for him to be put through his paces at an RAF fitness test. Finally, James takes one of the area's most abundant fish and makes mackerel and cauliflower with mango dressing.

programme.title: Love Your Garden
programme.desc: Alan Titchmarsh, David Domoney and Danny Clarke transform a small Leicester garden into a Caribbean-inspired technicolour paradise. Showing how colour can reinvigorate size or shape of garden, Alan and the boys' challenge is to create the perfect space for community worker Jules Richards, inspired by her love of Barbados. Meanwhile, in a separate garden Frances Tophill reveals how to use light coloured landscaping, shade-loving flowers and sculpture to bring beauty and vibrancy to a dark corner.

programme.title: Ainsley's Fantastic Flavours
programme.desc: Knocking up some tempting treats - and not just desserts - Ainsley makes some incredible dishes with a sweet twist! Caramelised, glazed and iced, perfect for those of us with a real sweet tooth, Ainsley makes Korean-inspired pork skewers and an American favourite with spicy and sweet buffalo sauce. Paralympic swimmer Ellie Simmonds pops in to show us how to make her family recipe for chocolate cheesecake, and Ainsley samples another Maltese classic.

programme.desc: In Donegal Town, Dermot's journey takes him further south along the Wild Atlantic Way, discovering a place where Irish tradition and global flavours sit side by side. His day begins at family-run Hannah Hats, where he's fitted in iconic Donegal tweed and learns why this rugged corner of Ireland became famous for its beautifully flecked fabric. Dressed fit for a fine meal, Dermot visits one of Ireland's most unexpected culinary hotspots: Chandpur, widely regarded as Ireland's best curry house. He meets Bangladeshi-born chef Rana, and together they cook railway curry using outstanding local Donegal lamb and potatoes - it's a heaven-made match of Asian flavours and quality Irish produce. For pudding, Dermot meets chef Brian McDermott, one of the biggest champions of Donegal's food scene. Together they bake a classic Irish apple pie, with Brian revealing why all the local rain creates richer grass, creamier milk and extra buttery pastry, making Donegal Town a dessert destination.

When the wife of a wealthy landowner is bludgeoned to death with a cricket bat, DCI Tom Barnaby and his team are enmeshed in a succession of calculating murders as blackmail, deceit, greed and revenge threaten to destroy Midsomer's tranquillity once again.

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: Detective series, based on the novels by Caroline Graham, that follows Inspector Barnaby as he investigates murder mysteries in Middle England. The sleepy village of Martyr Warren is invaded by quarrelsome New Age travellers, some of whom fall out with local magistrate Hector Bridges - the police are well aware of the tensions, but matters come to a head when Hector is found shot dead. It quickly appears that he was feared by almost everyone in sight - including his own family - and there is more to the travellers than meets the eye as one of them is a former British Army officer who fought alongside Hector in the Falklands War... Meanwhile, Barnaby is not feeling in full fighting trim for murder investigations as Joyce has put him on a strict diet to lose weight.

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: Feature-length drama about a detective whose patch is a seemingly idyllic rural district. When a local tramp is found murdered in the woods following a hunt meet, a local poacher is arrested and jailed - however, the young lad's father is then also brutally murdered and the killer attempts to pass it off as suicide. DCI Tom Barnaby and DS Troy realise that there is much more to this case than first appears as hidden within the hunt community are complex relationships, multiple lies, and incestuous pasts. With the hunt season in full swing, it is only a matter of time before someone else is savagely killed...

programme.title: Vera
programme.desc: Detective drama based on the novel of the same name by Ann Cleeves. Vera and the team investigate the case of a murdered social worker called Jenny Lister, a woman who was universally considered to have been principled and popular - in an overworked and understaffed social work system, a notorious case involving the death of a child seems to hold the key to solving the killing. Vera uses her innate empathy and intuition to pursue the truth behind the murder - when she discovers the real secret at the heart of Jenny's death, the killer will stop at nothing to keep it hidden.

programme.title: Hornblower
programme.desc: The first episode of a drama series about CS Forester's famous seafaring hero. Spithead, Portsmouth, 1793 - a storm is raging in the English Channel and a small shore boat is being lashed by squally rain as two oarswomen battle against the waves. Huddled at the stern is a pale-faced 17-year-old making his maiden voyage to a career in the Royal Navy - soaked to the skin in his ill-fitting uniform, doctor's son Horatio Hornblower steps aboard his first ship, the HMS Justinian. This shy and stuttering seaman is set to become the most gallant and redoubtable figure in naval history, but his peers are wary of his intelligence and malicious Midshipman Jack Simpson adds the new recruit to his list of targets - when Simpson accuses Hornblower of cheating at cards, Hornblower snaps and challenges Simpson to a duel to settle their differences once and for all. The other men think Horatio is mad, but they also think they know that Simpson is the best shot in the navy...
